---
title: "Graphical log-linear models from local margins"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Graphical log-linear models from local margins}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>")
library(gAtoms)
```

`fit_loglinear_graph()` fits a fixed undirected graphical model to complete
categorical observations. Graph vertex names must match data column names.
Factors retain declared levels, including unused categories. Characters and
integer/logical labels have deterministic frozen levels. Continuous numeric
columns and missing values are rejected. Sampling zeros are supported;
structural-zero constraints are not implemented.

```{r example}
G <- igraph::set_vertex_attr(igraph::make_ring(4, circular=FALSE),
                            "name", value=c("A","B","C","D"))
dat <- expand.grid(A=c("a","b"), B=c("x","y"),
                   C=c("u","v"), D=c("yes","no"))
dat <- dat[rep(seq_len(nrow(dat)), 1+seq_len(nrow(dat)) %% 4), ]
dec <- atom_decompose(G)
fit <- fit_loglinear_graph(dat, graph=G, decomp=dec)
fit
summary(fit)
logLik(fit)
deviance(fit)
fitted(fit, type="factorized")
```

Margins are aggregated directly from rows for the ordered atoms and separators;
no full Cartesian count table is created. Complete atoms and separators use
saturated closed-form estimates. Incomplete atoms use the selected engine:
`engine = "gRim"` (the default) calls `gRim::effloglin()` and `engine = "loglin"`
calls `stats::loglin()`; the requested engine is used as given and a failure is
reported as an error. Local fitted generator margins
must reproduce the observed margins. Iteration counts are `NA` when the engine
does not expose them.

Every local atom fit records which engine was requested and used:

```{r provenance}
summary(fit)$requested_engine
summary(fit)$fallback_count
summary(fit)$engine_provenance
```

`requested_engine` is the user request (`"gRim"` or `"loglin"`),
`attempted_engines` lists the engines that were actually executed in order,
`engine` is the engine that produced the fit, and `fallback` is `FALSE` with
`fallback_reason` `NA` because an explicit engine never falls back. When the
requested engine fails, the condition carries the failure in `attempted_engines`
and `engine_errors`.

Precomputed margins can be reused:

```{r sufficient}
ss <- margin_counts(dat, c(atoms(dec), separators(dec)))
fit2 <- fit_loglinear_graph(ss, G, decomp=dec)
logLik(fit2)
```

The global distribution is stored as atom probability factors divided by
separator factors. A zero separator margin implies zero global support, so
associated zero-over-zero configurations receive probability zero. Disconnected
components multiply independently.

`logLik()` reports the multinomial probability log-likelihood kernel

$$ \ell(\hat p) = \sum_x n_x \log \hat p(x), $$

conditional on the total sample size. The multinomial combinatorial constant
$\log(n!) - \sum_x \log(n_x!)$ is omitted. This omitted term is independent of
the fitted model and therefore cancels in likelihood-ratio deviances. Zero-count
cells contribute zero and are absent from the sum. Deviance uses sparse counts of
observed configurations. If a supplied statistics object lacks those counts,
deviance is unavailable. Model degrees of freedom and AIC/BIC are not provided.

Explicit full output returns **probabilities**, not counts:

```{r deliberately-small-full-table}
p <- fitted(fit, type="full")
sum(p)
fit$cells
```

Full output is guarded by `control$full_table_max_cells` (one million by default).
`force=TRUE` overrides that policy limit, but cannot override the supported array
size. Local tables have a separate `local_table_max_cells` guard. The default
factorized output remains usable for very large global state spaces.
`cells$full` is the theoretical Cartesian size; `total_local` and `max_local`
describe atom tables. `log_full` remains useful if the full product overflows.
